why:
The criterion holds. The must_not item forbids an issue that a build breaking plain CSV input could still pass. I checked whether any expect line guards CSV input when the flag is absent. One does: "Without --tsv, CSV behaviour is unchanged: printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js prints exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}]". It also checks that tabs are not treated as separators by default. A second line checks that the exported parse() keeps its comma default ("m.parse('a,b
1,2
')" prints [{"a":"1","b":"2"}]). Both lines have run proofs that a verifier can execute. Any build that broke plain CSV parsing in the CLI or in parse() would fail these lines. The output therefore does nothing on the must_not list.
